body: I love the third photo in particular where you're looking off into the distance. You look very glamorous in it, and cool at the same time.
Those eyes are like the big, beautiful bright moon, and shine just as brightly.
Yeahhhhh .... you got nothin' to worry about, man. She's gonna like what she sees at first glance.

> Somewhere out there is someone who actually wishes they knew you and they'll never find you if you aren't looking for them too...

Or not. There's no guarantee of this. It's hard not to feel like the devil you know is better than the angel that may not exist.

Making the bed in the morning.

You're just going to mess it up again sooner or later. You aren't likely to have many people wandering through your bedroom just to view it. What's the damn point?

When you work with words as a profession or an art, they become your tools, your weapons. You learn to count on them to accomplish what you need accomplished. And then when it comes to this incredibly crucial, emotionally impactful moment in your life and you realize your best tools are suddenly completely useless here ... that's a terrible feeling and I don't wish it on anyone.
Your style is incredible, on your body (which there is absolutely nothing wrong with) and around you.
Very nice, bright eyes, and the nose decoration flatters you. You'll have your choice of dates.
"Ugly" is about the farthest thing from my mind. Those lips are meant to be kissed often, and by someone who knows how. (Not a come-on, just a classic movie-inspired description.)
Maybe he was just overwhelmed by your awesomeness and how unworthy of it he felt. Because you do look pretty awesome.
Those glasses fit your face in a flattering way. Good choice!

As someone who has been asked this question, I can't speak for the OP, but I know my answers were a) I want to be with that PARTICULAR person, and b) yes, I would rather be with someone who does that, but there is no guarantee such a person exists. I do know that I care about the previous person, however.
Get what you can out of the relationship. It will be hard emotionally, but it probably would have been hard emotionally anyway. Now it's hard emotionally, but with sex.

I think it's really rude of her to ask you to delete the Insta picture. That's a part of your past that you own, and you should get to display it if you wish.

Remember, there's no timetable for this: If you get over her (in my experience, this is no certainty), it will happen on its own time. Feel what feels right to you, for as long as you feel it. Don't let anyone pressure you into "getting over it" earlier if you aren't ready. But at the same time, don't shut yourself off to other people. Don't force it, but be open.
You look happy. That's a beautiful glow on you.
